chapter: Vernon Andrade's band and Harlem life
title: Marriage, the Rhythm Club newsletter and writing
summary: Caldwell was married and separated, assistant secretary at the Rhythm Club, and wrote articles for its little book.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: They keep coming by and saying, no, don't do it. Why, you know, why don't you drop it (unintelligible), you know. Well, so that really kept you -- were you married by this time?
Yeah, I'd been married and separated.
Oh, you'd been married and separated by then?
Uh-huh.
Oh, I see. So you were really having a good life, I guess, huh?
Definitely.
What were you doing then in those days, just drinking and --
No, I was -- I was writing an article about the Rhythm Club. I was assistant secretary. Then we had a little old book we used to put out.
The Rhythm Club?
Yeah. And I used to write a lot for the club.
Well, how did you get to start writing?
Through Metcalf I started writing, through one of the fellows, one of the associate editors there at the time I was at the Rhythm Club.
It's most unusual for a musician to write because most of them hate writing letters even, don't they? I mean --
Well, I'm always -- like I can write 1,000 cards in less than a week. When I was in Copenhagen last

year on the concert, I wrote so many cards, the promoter said, hey, Hap, he said, you love to write, don't you? I say, well, I don't know where I inherited it from, but I always did. And I said -- I guess about 100 and some cards.
Well, but this little book at the Rhythm Club, what was that about?

Well, it was different (unintelligible) piano John Ross events that occur, like we had the Willie the Lion session there, (unintelligible) would come in there, Fats (unintelligible) would be playing, 'get up, you're not playing nothing. Let me get down there.' And, you know, lot of fun, you know, and like --
So you used to describe some of these?
Yeah, that's right.
Oh, I've never heard of those books (unintelligible). That's interesting.
Lot of musicians playing pool --
That's where you began your journalistic --
Uh-huh, that's where I begun then, ideas from there, and it was a lot of fun too. I publish -- when I say I'd write up sometimes --
(Laughter)
(Simultaneous remarks)
The reason I asked you if you were married, I was thinking, well, here you were with this band for three or four years, and, you know, you must have been having some sort of fun.
Oh, yes.
You know, because you were -- how old were you then? You were about -- just over 30.
That's right.
In your prime.
That's right. That's true.
